# TinyGame

> A pocket game console for kids and parents: a 320x172 screen, two endless clicky knobs, a tilt
> sensor, and games ("carts") written as single Lua 5.4 files with help from an AI.

To write a game, read the API card and copy patterns from the examples. New games go in `games/`.
Check every cart with `./tg check games/<name>.lua` (screenshot in `out/<name>.png`) before
sending it to the console with `./tg send games/<name>.lua`.

## Writing carts

- [API card](docs/api-card.md): everything a cart can use, the limits, and a list of things not to do
- [How to make a cart, step by step](AGENTS.md): the write, check, look and fix loop
- [Template](games/_template.lua): the starting point for a new game

## Example carts

- [Brick Bop](console/carts/brick.lua): sprites and a tile-map brick wall
- [Rock Dodge](console/carts/examples/rocks.lua): falling rocks, groups, tilt steering, saved best score
- [Tilt Roll](console/carts/examples/tilt.lua): a tilt maze with a knob fallback
- [WalkWalk](console/carts/examples/walkwalk.lua): a scrolling platformer
- [Snake](console/carts/examples/snake.lua): a grid game steered with knob notches
- [Knob Sketch](console/carts/examples/paint.lua): drawing with two knobs, shake to wipe

## Optional

- [Engine format details](docs/engine-v1.md): sprites and maps in more depth
- [Uploader](uploader/index.html): sends a cart to the console from Chrome or Edge
